entries.title: 1.2 The Grim World
entries.flavour: The world of Heraldry Skirmish is a realm of old faiths, broken kingdoms, hungry roads, and colder bargains. Kings, princes, bishops, and warlords still raise banners over land they can barely hold. They fight over relics, tolls, doctrine, trade roads, salt, iron, and pride. Their victories are measured in burnt farms and new taxes. Their defeats are carried by peasants who never chose a side.

entries.title: 1.3.2 The Six Climates of Ruin
entries.flavour: Beyond the walls, land has become allegiance. Expedition ledgers still say forest, city, cavern, ice, desert, and swamp. Survivors know better. They use older names. The shape of the world is plain enough to anyone who has walked it. The broken mountains run down its spine. The dead empire and its ruined cities sprawl across the eastern heart. The great forest spreads west to the salt-coast, the ice locks the north, the dunes burn in the south beyond the mountain passes, and the swamps drown the south-east where the rivers give out at the sea. The old imperial roads still join all of it, straight and patient, running out from the Ashlands to every climate that survived. A dry label cannot warn a traveller that a road has memory, a court still sits without lungs, or a pool of black water may be listening.

entries.title: The Greenmark
entries.flavour: The Greenmark is the great temperate forest of the surviving world. It is larger than the maps. Roots take a road within a season and make the mile-stones useless. Travellers report trees shifting at the edge of sight, upright hounds between trunks, and grove-circles where moss stays warm after snow. Foresters cut warning signs into bark for those who know how to read them. The most common sign means turn back even if the voice ahead is your own. The forest is no wilderness. It is a country that does not recognize human law.

entries.title: The Ashlands
entries.flavour: The Ashlands are the cities of the old empires after fire, law, and death finished with them. They sprawl across the eastern heart of the world, where the imperial roads still run out to every climate like spokes from a shattered wheel. Forums have collapsed into crypts. Temples lean over plazas filled with soot. Streets run black across districts no living guide will enter twice. Lamps still burn in shrines whose gods have no congregation. Patrols still cross boundaries that vanished before the current Bastions had names. The Ashlands are rich because whole treasuries died under stone. They are feared because the city still knows how to count.

entries.title: The Undermarches
entries.flavour: The Undermarches begin under every place that claims to have a foundation, and run deepest beneath the broken mountains at the world's centre. Mines break into older shafts. Older shafts open into tunnels no pick made. Surveyors return with maps that disagree with themselves. Wells sour overnight. Cellars breathe in winter. Borders on the surface mean little below, where passages run under rivers, burial hills, and walls the Bastions call secure. Down in the true dark the deep elves keep their own houses and their own law, older than any empire and crueller than any court that ever sat above. The deep does not need to invade. The surface keeps falling into it.

entries.title: The Pale City
entries.flavour: In the north, winter has become government. Cities that once held tens of thousands stand ice-locked, their gates frozen mid-closing. Towers crack in the cold. Courts, offices, processions, and taxes continue in forms no living citizen would recognize. Hearthhold sends parties north with oil, fire-charms, and instructions to leave tribute on the old road. No one agrees who first made that bargain. The snow covers ruin with clean hands. It heals nothing.

entries.title: The Sun-Drowned
entries.flavour: South of the broken mountains, the dunes have climbed over the wealthiest realms the world ever boasted of. Tomb-cities of the priest-kings break the horizon like teeth. Salt flats glitter where harbours stood. The desert leaves the dead in sight, enthroned, armoured, embalmed, or half-uncovered by wind. Saltspire's ledgers call the southern routes profitable. Its guides call them damned and charge for the difference. Under the sand, sealed courts keep their lamps lit.

entries.title: The Mire
entries.flavour: Where the southern rivers gave out before the sea, the swamps inherited the rest, spreading across the world's south-eastern lowlands. Bogs swallowed roads. Mangroves grew through village roofs. Stilt-houses lean over water that looks shallow until it opens. Reedmarch survives by toll, ferry, leechcraft, and denial. The hag-courts hold the deep fen, and they keep older bargains than any Bastion will admit to honouring. Everyone there knows The Mire is rising. No one profits from saying it aloud. The dead drift below the walkways. Sometimes they drift back.

brief.identity: The Mire, the southeastern swamps where rivers give out, where bogs swallowed roads and the dead drift below the walkways.
brief.composition: Water-level view along a plank walkway through a drowned village; mangroves grow through the roofs of stilt-houses, pale shapes drift beneath the surface.

entries.title: 1.3.3 The Six Bastions
entries.flavour: Each Bastion is a fortified holding: a walled town, a fortress-chapel, a sealed mining city, a stilt-town behind river-locks. None ruled before the Fall. They survived because they were small enough to be missed, lucky enough to be spared, or stubborn enough to close the gate while neighbours screamed outside. Now they are the great powers of what remains.
entries.direction: A great Bastion gate grinding shut at dusk, guards straining at the windlass inside while desperate figures outside reach for the closing gap.

brief.identity: The six Bastions survived the Fall by closing the gate while neighbours screamed outside.

entries.title: Greythorn
entries.flavour: Greythorn is a timber-walled town among ancient oaks at the last surviving crossroads of the western forest road. It endures because it pays the forest. Each autumn, tithe-bundles are left at the standing stones. Each spring, the gate-wardens count the foresters who returned, then count the tools of those who did not.

entries.title: Sablekeep
entries.flavour: Sablekeep is a fortified chapel-town built into the throat of a ruined imperial city, where the Ashlands meet the eastern edge of the forest and the old roads run straight on into the dead empire. It survives by burning. Consecrated braziers stand at every gate, bridge, and chapel window. They are never permitted to go out. The lower terraces rest on the bones of an older temple, and the bones are not all the right shape.

brief.identity: Sablekeep, a fortified chapel-town built into the throat of a ruined imperial city where the Ashlands meet the eastern forest, ruled by the Sable Watch, which survives by burning.
brief.composition: View from the straight imperial road looking up at the chapel-town climbing terraces in the throat of the ruined city; braziers burning at every gate, bridge and chapel window.

entries.title: Deepwarden
entries.flavour: Deepwarden is a sealed mining city carved into the foothills of the broken mountains. It survived the Fall by closing its great gate. Half the city was on the wrong side when it closed. The half that survived now lives in the upper terraces above what its people call simply the Dark.

brief.identity: Deepwarden, a sealed mining city carved into the foothills of the broken mountains, which survived by closing its great gate and now lives in upper terraces above the Dark.
brief.composition: View from the upper terraces down over the sealed great gate and into a black void below, the Dark; forge smoke rising behind and lantern lights dotted across the terraces.

entries.title: Hearthhold
entries.flavour: Hearthhold is a walled town in the high north, built around the Great Hearth that has burned without interruption since the Fall. If the Hearth goes out, Hearthhold dies: first the children, then the elderly, then everyone. Every resident takes a turn on the fire-watch. Children are taught to feed the flame before they are taught to read.

brief.identity: Hearthhold, a walled town in the high north built around the Great Hearth that has burned unbroken since the Fall; the smallest, poorest and bravest Bastion.
brief.composition: Interior view across a snowy square toward the Great Hearth, a vast stone fire-pit and chimney with a side-chamber chapel; a ring of walls and training ground behind.

entries.title: Saltspire
entries.flavour: Saltspire is a tower-city built around a deep, sacred well at the centre of an oasis ringed by salt-pans and the bones of older cities. It has the only reliable water for a hundred miles. This makes it wealthy. It also makes it hated.

brief.identity: Saltspire, a tower-city built around a deep sacred well at the centre of an oasis ringed by salt-pans and the bones of older cities; wealthy and hated.
brief.composition: Distant approach across salt-pans toward a cluster of tall towers around the oasis; caravans in the foreground, the sacred well-head at the heart.

entries.title: Reedmarch
entries.flavour: Reedmarch is a stilt-town raised over log pilings on a network of barges, ferry platforms, and toll bridges. It is the only crossing for 30 miles in any direction. Its people are ferrymen, smugglers, apothecaries, leech-tenders, and corpse-haulers. They know what is buried under their floors. They prefer not to discuss it.

brief.identity: Reedmarch, a stilt-town raised over log pilings on barges, ferry platforms and toll bridges; the only crossing for 30 miles, populated by ferrymen, smugglers, leech-tenders and corpse-haulers.
brief.composition: Water-level view from a ferry at the toll bridge, looking at the stilt-town with its patchwork of platforms and barges; a barge hall repositioned in the middle.

entries.title: 1.3.4 Magic in the Dying Lands
entries.flavour: The Five Traditions all survived the Fall. None survived intact.
entries.direction: A still life on a cracked altar: five damaged implements, one per tradition - a scorched spellbook, a chipped holy symbol, a bloodied ritual knife, a withered antler-and-holly charm, and a cracked crystal - each broken in its own way.

entries.title: 1.3.5 Monstrous Threats
entries.flavour: The Monsters of the Dying Lands are not scattered obstacles. They hold the world now. They keep roads closed, fields empty, shrines silent, and old borders meaningless. A village may vanish because of hunger, tax, fever, or weather. Outside the walls, those causes often have claws, banners, laws, or names.
entries.direction: An abandoned village street: claw-torn doors, an empty well, and a crude monster banner planted where the market cross once stood.

brief.identity: Monsters hold the Dying Lands now; they close roads, empty fields and set up their own banners.
brief.composition: An abandoned village street seen from one end in perspective, the market cross at the centre carrying a crude monster banner.

entries.title: 1.3.6 Adventurers and the Road
entries.flavour: Adventurers exist because the Bastions need work done beyond the reach of soldiers.
entries.direction: A small party walking out of a Bastion's postern gate along a muddy road, past a gibbet and a weathered warning post, toward a dark forest edge.

Muddy road with ruts and puddles

entries.title: 1.3.7 Legends and Echoes
entries.flavour: The Dying Lands remember. They do not remember kindly.
entries.direction: A barrow field at dusk where faint ghostly warriors of an ancient battle re-enact their last charge through the living grass, drawn only in sparse fine lines.

brief.identity: The Dying Lands remember: old battles and legends replay as echoes over the living ground.

A ghostly banner without device

entries.title: Human
entries.flavour: Humans are short-lived strivers who raise fragile things in a brutal world and call the result civilization. They learn fast, adapt faster, and persist in places that wear steadier peoples down to nothing.
entries.direction: A human traveller of a Bastion in layered road clothes with a pack, walking staff and short sword; ordinary, weathered and determined.

brief.identity: A Human adventurer, medium-sized, the plain short-lived 'striver' people who persist where steadier peoples fail, shown as a traveller in a Bastion's service.
brief.composition: Full figure in three-quarter view mid-stride along a rutted road, walking staff planted ahead, head turned back over the shoulder toward unseen pursuit.

Ordinary unremarkable face, stubble, weathered skin, determined set jaw

entries.title: Halfling
entries.flavour: Halflings keep to hearth smoke and hidden roads, and to the quiet wisdom of staying alive while larger folk blunder into the dark. They are small and quick, and far harder to break than strangers ever expect.
entries.direction: A halfling traveller in a hooded cloak with a sling, a well-kept pack and a cooking pot, alert and capable.

brief.identity: A Halfling adventurer, small-sized, hearth-and-hidden-roads folk who survive by staying unseen, shown as a capable traveller in a Bastion's service.

entries.title: Dwarf
entries.flavour: Dwarves are cut from sealed stone halls, old grudges, and craft traditions older than most fallen kingdoms. Hardship did not sour them so much as harden them, and little in this world meets one of them head-on and walks away whole.

brief.identity: A Dwarf adventurer, medium-sized but broad and heavy, from sealed stone halls and old craft traditions, shown as a hardened traveller in a Bastion's service.
brief.composition: Full figure in three-quarter view, braced wide-stanced at the top of a descending stair, lantern held forward into the dark in one hand, shield and handaxe ready in the other.

entries.title: Elf
entries.flavour: Elves are shaped by older forests and longer memories, and carry a grace that seems almost inhuman to the hurried peoples of the age. They move lightly, notice much, and bear the weight of beauty and loss without letting it show.
entries.direction: An elf traveller, tall and lean, in a long weathered cloak with a longbow and quiver, calm and watchful.

brief.identity: An Elf adventurer, medium-sized, tall and lean, a graceful, long-memoried traveller in a Bastion's service.

entries.title: Gnome
entries.flavour: Gnomes hold that every lock, mechanism, and buried device hides a lesson, and that the lesson is usually worth the risk of learning it. They are clever and precise, drawn to the exact dangers that sensible folk step around.
entries.direction: A gnome traveller with tinkering tools and lenses on a bandolier, a small crossbow and a heavy satchel.

brief.identity: A Gnome adventurer, small-sized, a clever, precise tinkerer drawn to dangerous devices, shown as a traveller in a Bastion's service.

entries.title: Goblin
entries.flavour: Goblins learn fast hands and quicker feet, and the plain truth that the weak survive by being where the blow is not. They fight mean, flee smart, and take every edge a hard world leaves lying about.
entries.direction: A goblin adventurer in a Bastion's employ: patched but well-kept leathers, a short blade and lantern, wary intelligence in the face; clearly a hired hero, not a raider.

brief.identity: A Goblin adventurer, small-sized, quick of hand and foot, shown as a hired hero in a Bastion's employ (an ally, not a raider).

entries.title: Orc
entries.flavour: Orcs are raised where weakness is punished at once and hesitation is never forgotten. Strength, momentum, and raw nerve have carried them this far, and they trust those three further than they trust subtlety.
entries.direction: An orc adventurer in a Bastion's employ: heavy travel-worn armour, a greataxe slung, scarred but composed; a sworn hireling, not a raider.

entries.title: Ratkin
entries.flavour: Ratkin come up from refuse heaps, tunnel warrens, and plague-alleys where numbers, speed, and hunger settled every argument. They know how to scatter, swarm, and strike where the enemy is already bleeding.
entries.direction: A ratkin adventurer in a hooded cloak and Bastion tabard, satchel of scavenged tools, bright watchful eyes; a hired hero, not a scavenger.

brief.identity: A Ratkin adventurer, small-sized, quick and swarming folk of refuse heaps and warrens, shown as a hired hero in a Bastion's service.

entries.title: Deep Elf
entries.flavour: Deep elves are a crueller branch of the elder blood, raised on night, venom, and treachery taught as a fine art. They are graceful and dangerous, and far more at ease beneath the dark than beneath the sun.
entries.direction: A deep elf adventurer who has come to the surface: pale skin, a hood pulled against daylight, fine dark armour and a curved blade; an outcast hireling, not a warrior of the deep courts.

brief.identity: A Deep Elf adventurer, medium-sized, an outcast of the cruel night-bred branch of the elder blood who has come to the surface as a hireling.

entries.title: Demonborn
entries.flavour: Something infernal stains the demonborn line, whether by old pact, curse, or ancestral trespass. Doors do not open for them, but fire parts, fear bends, and darker powers sometimes answer when they are called.
entries.direction: A demonborn traveller with small horns, a tail and ember-like eyes, dressed in a plain pilgrim's cloak.

brief.identity: A Demonborn adventurer, medium-sized, of infernal-stained blood, shown as a plain-cloaked pilgrim traveller in a Bastion's service.

entries.title: Drakeblood
entries.flavour: The drakeblood carry the remnant of an older majesty in the blood, as blessing, burden, or half-remembered debt. The world is fallen, but power still answers them in the old language of flame, storm, and scale.
entries.direction: A drakeblood traveller with scaled skin along jaw and hands and a ridge of small horns, in a heavy cloak with a spear.

brief.identity: A Drakeblood adventurer, medium-sized, carrying the remnant of an older dragon majesty in the blood, shown as a heavily cloaked traveller in a Bastion's service.

entries.title: Bugbear
entries.flavour: Seven feet of shaggy, long-armed menace with a flat face and fur the colour of dead bracken, the bugbear moves through the undergrowth in a silence it has no right to. It strikes from arm's reach before its quarry knows it is there, rising out of cover with a spiked morningstar already swinging. It much prefers the ambush to the open fight. Where bugbears lair, goblins serve as their terrified scouts.

entries.title: Harpy
entries.flavour: Half-mortal and half-carrion-bird, the harpy nests in the Greenmark's broken towers and sings travellers off the road and into its talons. The song is a lure that no resolve fully shakes. Up close it is filth and hooked claws, shrieking as it rakes. Its hunger is older than the Fall, and it was never once satisfied.

entries.title: Goblin Shaman
entries.flavour: Hung with fetishes of bone and crow-feather, the goblin shaman is the one goblin its own kind fears more than the enemy. It hangs behind the mob and spits hexes that wither courage and rot resolve. Its magic is small and spiteful, scavenged from older powers it does not begin to understand. Kill it, and the warband's nerve tends to break with it.

entries.title: Bandit Captain
entries.flavour: The bandit captain held a real commission once, or says so often enough to be believed. Armoured in looted mail and barking orders a crew will actually follow, they turn a rabble into something that fights like soldiers. They parry the first blow, answer the second, and spend their underlings freely to keep their own skin whole. Greythorn carries a standing bounty on three of them by name.

entries.title: Dire Bear
entries.flavour: The dire bear is the Greenmark grown teeth, a shaggy mountain of muscle that stands twice a man's height and swats deadwood aside to reach whatever it has smelled. It mauls with both forepaws and finishes with a bite that splits shields. Hunters who corner one rarely walk home. It bears no malice; it is only enormous, and always hungry.

entries.title: Blood Ape
entries.flavour: Slab-shouldered and crimson-furred, the blood ape knuckles through the high canopy and drops onto anything that bleeds. It fights in a building frenzy, both fists hammering faster as its own wounds mount, so the redder it grows the harder it hits. They hold the upper branches of the deep Greenmark and suffer no rival to share them.

entries.title: Gorebeak Bear
entries.flavour: Body of a bear, head and foreclaws of a great owl, the gorebeak is a stitched-together horror of the deep wood, its hooked beak punching clean through plate. It pins prey with raking claws and worries at the gap until something gives. Whether the burning years made these or merely woke them, the foresters cannot agree. The argument is no comfort to the pinned.

entries.title: Ogre
entries.flavour: Twice a man's height and slope-shouldered, an ogre is a slab of grey muscle and gut bound in stitched hides. It claims a ford or a narrow run between the trees and takes a toll of all that try to pass. It does not count coin. It counts the heavy, bright things its last few meals were carrying, and swings a tree-trunk club to collect more.

entries.title: Dryad Grovewarden

It steps between trunks as though they were doorways and binds intruders in grasping root. The Antlered Warden's tithe keeps most groves quiet. Where it goes unpaid, the grovewardens stir.

entries.title: Forest Troll
entries.flavour: Gangling, moss-slick, and stinking of the bog-edge, the forest troll is all reaching arms and a mouth of broken tusks. Its wounds knit shut before the blood has dried, and only fire or acid puts one down to stay. It is stupid, relentless, and forever hungry. Greythorn's woodcutters carry oil for exactly one reason.

entries.title: Werewolf
entries.flavour: A haunted villager by day, a hunched grey killer at the turning of need, the werewolf carries an old curse in its blood. Mundane steel slides from its hide; only silver and magic bite true. It strikes from the treeline and is gone before the screaming stops, then circles back for the wounded. Every bitten survivor is tomorrow's werewolf.

entries.title: Green Dragon
entries.flavour: Apex predator of the Greenmark and its oldest liar, the green dragon is a serpentine tyrant the colour of deep moss, spine-crested, its breath a rolling, corrosive poison. It does not rampage; it manipulates, ruling a swathe of forest through fear and bargain. Lesser things bring it tribute in exchange for being spared a while longer.

entries.title: Undead Warrior
entries.flavour: The Ashlands never disbanded its legions; it merely let them die unburied. An undead warrior is a skeleton or half-rotted corpse in the rusted kit of the old empire, still holding the post it was set to generations back. It fights in ragged ranks, shield to shield, mindless but drilled by sheer habit. There are always more of them in the ash.

entries.title: Undead Crossbowman
entries.flavour: Behind the shambling battle-line stand the crossbowmen, dead marksmen cranking warped windlasses with fleshless fingers. They loose in volleys at whatever their soldiers have fixed in place, and their bolts seek the gaps in armour with horrible patience. They do not tire, flinch, or lose their nerve. entries.title: Ghoul
entries.flavour: Grey, gaunt, and hook-clawed, a ghoul is what hunger makes of a corpse that would not lie still. It lopes in packs through the Ashlands' tombs, and its bite carries a paralytic rot that stiffens the limbs. Ghouls take the living and the freshly dead alike, and they are clever enough to cut off the straggler. They were people once, before the long famine that came after the cities burned.

entries.title: Possessed Corpse

A possessed corpse is a body worn by something that crept in from the dark between worlds, lurching on borrowed legs toward a wrong, jerking purpose. Its grip does not tire, and it bursts in a reek of corruption when it finally falls. Whatever rides it does not speak. It only reaches.

entries.title: Ember Skull

It spits gouts of fire at the living from beyond their reach. Old grimoires name them the failed apprentices of the empire's pyromancers, kept burning by their final spite. Snuff the flame and the skull drops inert.

entries.title: Wererat
entries.flavour: Where the Ashlands meet the old sewers and undercrofts, the wererat thrives, a hunched, plague-grey shapeshifter scurrying between man and rat-thing. It bites, then skitters back into the dark, leaving filth-fever in every wound. Mundane blades barely mark it. One wererat is a nuisance; a nest of them is an outbreak.

entries.title: Spectre

It passes through wall and armour alike, and its touch drinks the warmth and the years out of the living. Steel finds nothing to bite; only silver and magic answer. The ruined city is thick with them, each one a question that was never answered.

A sentinel plants itself in a breach and will not be shifted, lending its iron stillness to the lesser dead around it. It does not pursue. It only holds, forever, a line that fell centuries ago.

A forsaken archer draws a cursed longbow with a dead marksman's precision, and its arrows leave a clinging curse where they strike. Smoke and shadow do not trouble its aim. It parries with a lifetime's drill written into bone and cannot be slowed or turned aside. Bound by an oath it can no longer recall, it follows Veyr's banner into every fight. Its honour has curdled into compulsion.

entries.title: Forsaken Duelist
entries.flavour: Faster than a dead thing has any right to be, the forsaken duelist fights with a single flashing rapier and a fencer's lethal economy. It waits for a blade to commit, slips the strike, and answers through the opening. In life it was the empire's finest fencer; in death it is the same, only tireless. Veyr keeps the duelists close, for they punish every misjudged swing.

entries.title: Basilisk
entries.flavour: Heavy and eight-legged and the size of an ox, the basilisk drags itself through the Ashlands' rubble behind a gaze that turns flesh slowly to stone. Meet its eyes and the stiffening starts, the limbs first, then the rest. Even its blood petrifies whatever it touches. The ruins are dotted with its leavings, statues of the surprised, caught mid-stride.

It hunts that grudge across the Ashlands with tireless focus, and struck down it claws upright again to land a final blow. Cross its path and you become the grudge. It does not stop until you do.

entries.flavour: The empire's master-smiths forged iron golems to outlast the dynasty, and in that one task they grimly succeeded. A towering automaton of riveted black iron, it shrugs off blade and spell alike and answers with piledriver fists. Magic washes from its plates; edged steel skids away. It guards a throne whose claimant is centuries of dust.

entries.title: Lich
entries.flavour: A lich is an archmage who refused death and paid for the refusal in everything that made them human. A desiccated sorcerer-king in mouldering finery, they command the Ashlands' dead with a gesture and loose blasts of soul-rending necrosis. Destroy the body and they re-form, so long as the hidden phylactery endures. The empire fell. Its worst survivor did not.

One alone is nothing; a chittering mob of them, dragging traps and loosing slings from the dark, is a real danger. They know every tunnel and trust not one. It guards avenues that have not seen a living census in centuries. The cold preserves it whole; it will hold that post when the last warm thing in the world goes out. There are always more under the snow.

entries.title: Snow Goblin
entries.flavour: Gaunt and white-furred, snow goblins den in the Pale City's drifts and tunnels, ambushing out of the whiteout with frost-edged knives. They are invisible against the snow until the moment they move. Cowardly and quick, they strip the frozen dead and bolt from any honest fight. The scavengers are their lowest caste, scrawny twitching things in matted grey fur, darting through the ruins to strip anything not frozen to the ground. They swarm, they scurry, and they rarely stand to fight. Where the scavengers pick, the warren is never far behind.

It runs in packs that herd prey into the open, where the wind does half the killing. Its bite carries the chill of the Pale City itself. entries.title: Skeleton Archer
entries.flavour: The archers of the priest-king tombs stand in alcoves carved to fit them, bows still strung after centuries. The arrows have not rotted; some things are kept by intention, others by spite. They loose in disciplined volleys at whatever the skeleton warriors have engaged. Their aim is exactly as good as it was the day they died.

entries.title: Mummy
entries.flavour: A priest-king's preserved corpse risen in wrath, the mummy comes bound in resin-soaked wrappings and trailing the dread of a dead god's authority. Its touch lays a withering curse, and the mere sight of it can root a victim in terror. Fire is its one true fear. It guards a tomb whose treasures it will not share, not even now.

It runs prey to ground across the open sand and tears with bony jaws. No flesh means no fatigue and no fear. The tomb-courts loose them like hounds.

entries.title: Wind Elemental
entries.flavour: A howling spiral of desert air turned malevolent, the wind elemental is a near-invisible vortex that flings sand and bodies with equal ease. It buffets foes off their feet and is barely troubled by ordinary weapons. It haunts the open wastes where the Sun-Drowned's storms are born. You hear it long before the sand begins to bite.

entries.title: Desert Naga
entries.flavour: A great serpent with an almost-human face and the patient cunning of something very old, the desert naga coils among the tomb-pillars. It spits venom from a distance and crushes what comes close, hexing the strong to leave them weak. The priest-kings kept them as guardians and oracles. They guard still. They no longer answer.

entries.title: Fire Elemental
entries.flavour: A roaring man-shape of living flame, white-hot at the core and shedding embers at the edges, the fire elemental sets alight everything it touches and scorches whatever strikes it. Water and ice are its only checks; the desert sun is its cradle. It draws a trail of cinders across the tomb-floors. To lay hands on it is to burn.

entries.title: Giant Skeleton
entries.flavour: A looming framework of fused bone twice a man's height, the giant skeleton is what remains of something that was never entirely natural and is far less so now. It moves with grinding deliberation, sweeping aside anything in its path with fists like falling masonry. Tomb-city carvings show its kind kneeling before the priest-kings; none show them standing. Whatever it was raised to guard, it guards it still.

entries.title: Medusa
entries.flavour: A serpent-haired figure whose gaze turns the living slowly to stone, the medusa lurks among the statues that were once its admirers. It fights with blade and venomous snake-hair, but its eyes are what fill the tomb-galleries with permanent witnesses. The priest-kings cursed its kind, or rewarded them; the tales cannot agree. Their victims cannot say.

entries.title: Tomb Necromancer

A tomb necromancer is a withered figure in the faded regalia of a dead bureaucracy, raising the buried to enforce statutes no living court remembers. It withers the living with a gesture and calls up the dead to fill the gaps in its ranks. Everything it administers belongs to a world that ended.

entries.flavour: A warty, weed-haired crone, the swamp hag poles their way through The Mire cursing all they meet, slipping half into the spirit-world when cornered. Their stench chokes out hope. entries.flavour: A many-headed reptilian horror, the hydra wallows in The Mire's deepest pools, each serpentine neck striking on its own and snapping at anything in reach. It cannot be frightened, and it bites back the instant something draws near. Cut a head away and it simply works with the others. It is the apex even the crocodiles fear.

entries.title: The Ancient Void Dragon

For centuries it has marched the same patrol, defending an empire that no longer exists. Nothing has yet proven able to stop it.

Its acid breath strips flesh from bone, and at its will the waters rise to swallow the ground its enemies stand on. It takes tribute from every settlement in the mire and devours those who come up short. The bells of its cathedral toll underwater, and the frogs have not sung there in living memory.

entries.title: Scenario 1: Hunt the Wild Beast
entries.flavour: Something out of the deep wood has taken Greythorn's logging camps for its hunting ground, and with them the timber the Bastion is built on. The first deaths were blamed on dire wolves. The next were found driven through splintered palisade timbers, which dire wolves do not manage. Its pelt, skull, and teeth would buy a season behind the walls, and the Council of Captains will pay either way to have the camps cutting again. Comfort and timber have sent both parties into the trees.

The standing stones hum when no wind passes, and pale lights move between them on moonless nights. Greythorn's farmers leave bread there and do not look back. Scholars call it a site of power. The Council of Captains calls it part of the tithe, and pays it without complaint.

entries.title: Scenario 3: The Bandit's Toll

A toll crew has claimed a bend of the trail and nailed its prices to the trees in stolen blood. Caravans wait behind palisades while bread grows dear inside Greythorn's walls. The Council of Captains has stamped a bounty and sent it out with anyone hungry enough to answer.

entries.title: Scenario 4: The Spider's Silk Route
entries.flavour: Silk-traders whisper of a ravine in the deep Greenmark where the webs hold steel like thread and fetch absurd prices in Bastion markets. The spinners are the Broodmother's daughters, strayed up from the dark, and the place is on no honest map. That has not stopped a Greythorn merchant from selling the same path through the thorns to two parties at once.

entries.title: Scenario 5: The Ambushed Emissary
entries.flavour: An emissary vanished on the western forest road carrying documents sealed under two rival Bastion laws. One patron in Greythorn wants the courier found breathing. entries.title: Scenario 1: The Fallen Observatory
entries.flavour: A star-engine once crowned these ruins, and its broken brass arms still turn when moonlight enters the cracked dome. Wizards would give a finger for the instruments scattered across the shifting floors, which is precisely why the Sable Watch wants them carried to Sablekeep and locked away from unregistered hands. The old servants of the place still know the penalty for touching them. They have a great deal of time in which to enforce it.

entries.title: 11.1 Campaign Overview
entries.flavour: A Stronghold is not a castle in the noble sense. No ancient bloodline sanctifies it. No bard remembers its founding. Its stones come from ruined shrines, abandoned watch-keeps, broken bridges, and walls that failed other people first. Its gates are paid for with burial gold, bounty coin, chapel debt, and the last wages of the dead.

entries.flavour: The Chapel is small, cold, and crowded with votive offerings from those who survived by inches. Its saints are chipped. Its relics are suspect. Its candles burn low even when no wind enters.

entries.title: The Expedition Hall
entries.flavour: The Expedition Hall is packed earth, split posts, blunted steel, blood in the mud, and shouted correction from veterans with no patience for heroic stupidity. New recruits learn quickly that courage is not a defence.

entries.flavour: The Undercroft is a warren of cellars, sealed drains, hidden doors, and passages older than the Stronghold above it. Smugglers, informants, and quiet killers all find reasons to know its shape.
